cues.en: Instructor: This section of the course is all about normalizing or standardizing your data and identifying and possibly removing outliers from your data.
cues.zh: 講師：這一章會介紹如何將資料正規化或標準化，以及如何找出資料中的離群值，並在適當時移除。

cues.en: This is related to issues of cleaning your data and processing your data, which is really important for many statistical analyses and for machine learning.
cues.zh: 這涉及資料清理和資料處理，對很多統計分析和機器學習都非常重要。

cues.en: You'll see, in fact several examples when we get to some machine learning applications of how you can get incorrect results if your data are not appropriately normalized
cues.zh: 事實上，談到機器學習應用時，你會看到好幾個例子，說明如果沒有適當地將資料正規化

cues.en: or standardized, or if you have large outliers in the data.
cues.zh: 或標準化，或資料中存在很大的離群值，就可能得到錯誤結果。

cues.en: So I'm gonna kick this off with a video called garbage in, garbage out, which is typically abbreviated to GIGO.
cues.zh: 因此，我先用這部名為「垃圾進，垃圾出」的影片開場，通常簡稱 GIGO。

cues.en: And basically what this means, this phrase, this means that if you start with crappy data, you're going to get crappy results.
cues.zh: 這句話基本上就是說，如果一開始用的資料很糟，得到的結果也會很糟。

cues.en: And, okay, so here are two comics that I like out of many from XKCD.
cues.zh: 這裡是 XKCD 眾多漫畫中，我很喜歡的兩則。

cues.en: You can pause the video if you want to spend some time reading them.
cues.zh: 如果想花點時間閱讀，可以暫停影片。

cues.en: But essentially this one is about machine learning.
cues.zh: 這一則基本上是在談機器學習。

cues.en: And the idea here of this little dialogue is that if you take an approach in data analysis, statistics, and machine learning and deep learning,
cues.zh: 這段小對話想表達的是，進行資料分析、統計、機器學習和深度學習時，

cues.en: if you take an approach of just pouring your data without any thought into some big pile of analyses that you may not even understand, you're going to get results
cues.zh: 如果只是毫不思考地把資料倒進一大堆分析方法裡，甚至連這些分析都不理解，那麼得到的結果

cues.en: that you also don't know how to interpret.
cues.zh: 也會讓你不知道該如何解讀。

cues.en: And the main point of this comic over here is that if you start, if you include garbage with junk, crappy, noisy data into an equation,
cues.zh: 另一則漫畫的重點是，如果一開始把垃圾、劣質、充滿雜訊的資料放進方程式裡，

cues.en: the result is basically always going to be garbage no matter what you do.
cues.zh: 不管怎麼做，結果基本上都還是垃圾。

cues.en: The general conclusion of GIGO is that awful data leads to awful results.
cues.zh: GIGO 的整體結論是，糟糕的資料會導致糟糕的結果。

cues.en: There is no fancy pants, super cool, sophisticated data analysis method that runs on some cluster of GPUs that can compensate
cues.zh: 沒有任何花俏、酷炫、複雜，甚至在 GPU 叢集上執行的資料分析方法，能夠彌補

cues.en: for really bad data.
cues.zh: 真正糟糕的資料。

cues.en: If you have bad data, if you start with awful data, noisy data, missing data, if you start with just a bad data set, you are guaranteed
cues.zh: 如果資料不好，一開始就是糟糕的資料、充滿雜訊的資料、有缺漏的資料，如果用的就是一組很差的資料，那麼無論如何，都必然

cues.en: to get awful results no matter what.
cues.zh: 得到糟糕的結果。

cues.en: So that's really problematic.
cues.zh: 這是個很嚴重的問題。

cues.en: You have to be mindful of starting with good, clean, high quality data.
cues.zh: 你必須留意，一開始就要有良好、乾淨、高品質的資料。

cues.en: Of course, the converse of this statement isn't necessarily true.
cues.zh: 當然，這句話的反過來不一定成立。

cues.en: So having awesome data doesn't guarantee getting awesome results.
cues.zh: 也就是說，擁有極好的資料，並不保證得到極好的結果。

cues.en: You might have really beautiful data, but your hypothesis is not correct, so then you're not gonna get the results that you expect.
cues.zh: 資料可能非常漂亮，但你的假設不正確，因此得不到預期結果。

cues.en: But it certainly is the case that bad data leads to uninterpretable results.
cues.zh: 不過，糟糕的資料確實會導致無法解讀的結果。

cues.en: So whenever absolutely possible, start with clean data.
cues.zh: 所以，只要有可能，就從乾淨的資料開始。

cues.en: Now, I wish I could just give you a set of instructions, fool proof instructions that anyone could follow to guarantee that you will have clean data.
cues.zh: 我希望能直接給你一套萬無一失、任何人照著做就能保證取得乾淨資料的操作步驟。

cues.en: But unfortunately that is simply not possible, and that is because the appropriate strategies for cleaning and normalizing data are very much dependent
cues.zh: 但很可惜，這根本不可能，因為適當的資料清理與正規化策略，高度取決於

cues.en: on the specific application, the specific discipline that you're working in, what you're doing with the data, how the data were collected and so on.
cues.zh: 具體應用、所處領域、要如何使用資料、資料如何收集等等。

cues.en: So cleaning data and getting clean data is quite idiosyncratic to each individual experiment, or sometimes each individual dataset.
cues.zh: 因此，如何清理資料和取得乾淨資料，對每個實驗，有時甚至對每組資料，都有各自的特殊性。

cues.en: But what I can say more generally is that you should always, to the extent possible, be meticulous, critical, patient, and unbiased when you are cleaning your data.
cues.zh: 但比較一般性的建議是，清理資料時，應該盡可能細心、保持批判思考、有耐心，而且不帶偏見。

cues.en: So now you know what a GIGO is, it's garbage in, garbage out.
cues.zh: 現在你知道 GIGO 是什麼了，就是垃圾進，垃圾出。

cues.en: And essentially the idea is that you have to start with good, clean data before you start doing your analyses.
cues.zh: 基本概念是，開始分析之前，必須先有良好、乾淨的資料。

cues.en: If you have crappy data, you're not going to get good results.
cues.zh: 資料很糟，就不會有好的結果。

cues.en: Having clean data and cleaning data generally requires human expertise and some familiarity with the particular topic area that you are working in with the nature of the data
cues.zh: 擁有乾淨的資料，以及進行資料清理，通常需要人的專業判斷，也需要熟悉你所研究的特定領域，以及正在處理的資料

cues.en: that you are working with.
cues.zh: 本身的性質。

cues.en: There are no generic one size fits all methods that are going to guarantee clean data for any kind of dataset.
cues.zh: 沒有一種通用、放諸四海皆準的方法，能保證任何類型的資料集都變得乾淨。
